newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt sees no delay in CVRD auction - Kandir.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt sees no delay in CVRD auction - Kandir.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the government was not expecting any delays in the privatization auction of state minining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
A strategic 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares will be sold off at auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange April 29 for a minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
Asked whether there would be a delay if only one consortium decided to bid for CVRD at the auction, Kandir said: "We are not working with the hypothesis that there will be a delay."
He said the CVRD sale would still be good business for the government even if the 45 percent block of shares was sold for only the minimum price.

"This is the first time a minimum price has been set above the proposals of privatization consultants," Kandir said. "When the government set the minimum price, it took into consideration all the proposals as well as the market price of the company over the last 90 days."
He said the government was expecting two consortia to bid for CVRD.
"Our expectation is that a second consortium will be formed," he said. "CSN is working to form a second consortium and I think in the next two weeks this consortium will be established."

A consortium including Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim, Japan's Nippon Steel Corp, South Africa's Anglo American Corp and Banco Safra is widely seen as the most advanced and the favorite for buying the CVRD stake.

Brazil's largest steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) has also said it is also determined to bid on CVRD, but is still looking for new alliances after two potential partners, retail bank Bradesco and South Africa's Gencor Ltd dropped out of the race.

CSN is said to be in talks with Banco Garantia, Garantia Participacoes, the Suzano paper and pulp group, the Soros Fund, Japanese trading company Mitsubishi Corp and the Brazilian engineering group Camargo Correa.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
